definition: Building software primarily by describing what you want in natural language and letting an AI write the code, with the human steering rather than typing every line.
details: Popularized by Andrej Karpathy in 2025, the term describes a flow where the developer prompts, reviews and iterates on AI-generated code — “fully giving in to the vibes” — while the model handles syntax, boilerplate and edits.
story: Imagine learning a language by reading every book in the library and noticing, over time, which words travel together. It does not memorize a rulebook; it absorbs a library. The machine learns language the way you did — by hearing so much of it that the patterns sink in. It is fluency built from pattern, not from memorized rules. That pattern-earned fluency is Vibe Coding.
